newsitem.title: EGYPT: Kuwaiti minister briefs Egypt on Gulf events.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaiti minister briefs Egypt on Gulf events.

text.p: Kuwaiti Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Saud al-Sabah briefed Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Tuesday on Kuwait's role in the confrontation between Iraq and the United States.
Sheikh Saud left Kuwait around dawn as part of a Kuwaiti diplomatic initiative to win support for its decision to let the U.S. forces reinforce in Kuwait and the Gulf.
Egyptian troops helped drive Iraqi forces out of Kuwait in 1991 but Cairo has not been enthusiastic about this month's U.S. attacks on targets in Iraq.
It says the pretext -- an offensive in northern Iraq by a Kurdish faction backed by Baghdad -- was quite different from that of 1991, when Iraqi troops occupied a foreign state.

Egyptian Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif told reporters after the meeting in Alexandria: "President Mubarak reiterated Egypt's support for Kuwait and its right to defend its sovereignty and secure its homeland in the past and the future. Egypt's position on this matter has not changed."
Sheikh Saud is expected to fly on to Syria, which also contributed troops to the multinational alliance in 1991.
Egypt, Syria and the six Gulf Cooperation Council states are the members of the loose regional grouping which signed the Damascus Declaration after the Gulf war.
